newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. vote on Jerusalem a declaration of war -PLO.
newsitem.headline: U.S. vote on Jerusalem a declaration of war -PLO.

text.p: Palestinians on Thursday described as a declaration of war a non-binding U.S. House of Representatives resolution calling on President Bill Clinton to reaffirm that Jerusalem must remain Israel's "undivided capital".

Israel, which captured Arab East Jerusalem in 1967 and annexed it in a move unrecognised by the international community including the United States, expressed satisfaction at Tuesday's 406-17 vote in favour of the Sense of Congress resolution.

The vote, which does not oblige the Clinton administration to act, came as Egypt struggled to resolve a peacemaking crisis between Israel and the PLO spurred by Israel's beginning work in March on a 6,500-home Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

"This decision will leave a dark shadow on security and stability in the Middle East and in Palestine. It is a clear call for violence and settlements at the same time," Ahmed Abdel-Rahman, general secretary of the Palestinian Authority cabinet, told Reuters.

"Recognising the annexation of Jerusalem to Israel and opening an embassy there without recognising East Jerusalem as the capital of Palestine is a declaration of war on the Palestinian people," he said.

In October 1995, the U.S. Senate and the House passed the Jerusalem Embassy Act which states as a matter of U.S. policy that Jerusalem should remain "the undivided capital of Israel" and that the American embassy should be moved there by May 1999.
But, recognising the volatility of the issue of Jerusalem, it allowed Clinton to suspend the embassy's move from Tel Aviv for six-month periods.
"American policy, which is well known on this issue, has not changed," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said on Wednesday.
He said it was important the United States not take "pre-emptive measures or unilateral measures...that might complicate isues pertaining to Jerusalem".
Palestinians say Israeli settlements pre-empt final negotiations which are to include the status of Jerusalem. They want Arab East Jerusalem as capital of a future state.
Palestinian Legislative Council Speaker Ahmed Korei, also known as Abu Ala, later told a news conference the Authority was awaiting Clinton's reaction to the resolution.

"We hope...President Clinton will stop this resolution and will refuse it," Korei said in English. "Nobody can understand such a resolution to be taken in this critical time while the peace process is facing a real impasse."
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's media adviser David Bar-Illan hailed the vote.
"I think the fact of a massive majority like that, of 406 against 17 voting to declare Jerusalem as the united capital of Israel, cannot be ignored," Bar-Illan told Israel's army radio.
"The majority of the world cannot ignore the fact that the American people has expressed its will in this most explicit and clear manner."
Costa Rica and El Salvador are the only countries with embassies in Jerusalem.
